[word/document.xml] Construction and Field Operations Manual

[word/document.xml] The nominal 4 ft x 8 ft sideline screen provides the color guard with a concealed area for storing equipment and making costume or equipment changes. The frame is constructed from 3/4-in. EMT conduit, off-the-shelf brackets, and 3D-printed parts. Decorative vinyl covers the finished face. The completed screen folds flat for transport and storage and unfolds for field deployment.

+[word/document.xml] This section governs the preparation, alignment, dual-axis tensioning, and mechanical fastening of the custom printed vinyl coverings to completed sideline screen frames. Installing vinyl on the folding frame requires a clean staging area, careful bleed centering, double-sided tape adhesion, and mechanical clamping with greenhouse snap clamps to prevent loosening under high field wind loads.
+[word/document.xml] Recommended Vinyl Dimensions & Ordering Specifications

+[word/document.xml] Sideline screen face coverings are custom-ordered commercial vinyl banners. Because the screens are positioned directly along the field boundary facing stadium audiences and adjudicators, the printed artwork must be oriented right-reading and centered precisely across the outer EMT conduit frame.

+[word/document.xml] Required Materials & Fastening Hardware
+[word/document.xml] Assemble all necessary staging items, adhesive consumables, and retention hardware before initiating vinyl mounting on a frame:

+[word/document.xml] • Moving blankets: Two to three clean, heavy-duty moving blankets or carpet runners spread across the shop floor to cushion the printed vinyl face against dust, grit, and concrete abrasion.

+[word/document.xml] • Custom vinyl banner: One custom printed outdoor banner per screen, rolled with print side facing inward. Unroll and inspect for print flaws and correct orientation prior to assembly.

+[word/document.xml] • Double-sided tape: 1-in. wide heavy-duty outdoor mounting tape (Appendix B Index [9]). Cut into sixteen (16) strips of approximately 4-in. length (~64 linear inches per screen). Application schedule: 5 strips on each long rail (10 total) and 3 strips on each short rail (6 total). Tape quantities are provisional (TBD) and will be validated during build testing.

+[word/document.xml] • Greenhouse snap clamps: Sixteen (16) 1-in. greenhouse clamp clips (Appendix B Index [8]). Snapped directly over the wrapped vinyl at every tape location (5 along each long rail, 3 along each short rail). Note: While the frame uses 3/4-in. trade size EMT conduit, EMT has an actual outer diameter of approximately 0.922 in. (nearly 1 in. OD); wrapped with vinyl and tape, 1-in. greenhouse snap clamps provide the proper snug snap fit.

+[word/document.xml] • Surface preparation (Optional): Isopropyl alcohol (IPA) and clean microfiber cloth. Degreasing the conduit is completely optional—the heavy-duty tape combined with mechanical greenhouse snap clamps provides more than enough holding power. A weaker initial adhesive bond to the bare conduit is actually preferable, as it significantly simplifies tape removal and cleanup later.
+[word/document.xml] • Personnel: Two (2) persons minimum for staging and long-side wrapping; three (3) persons recommended during short-side tensioning so opposite ends can be pulled simultaneously.
+[word/document.xml] Step-by-Step Vinyl Installation Procedure
+[word/document.xml] Step 1: Staging and Surface Protection

+[word/document.xml] Thoroughly sweep and vacuum a clean, flat floor area measuring at least 10 ft x 14 ft. Lay moving blankets flat across the entire work zone to prevent grit from scratching the printed graphic.
+[word/document.xml] Carefully unroll the custom vinyl banner face down directly on top of the moving blankets. Inspect the reverse side for cleanliness and smooth out any major packing rolls.
+[word/document.xml] Step 2: Frame Placement and Bleed Alignment
+[word/document.xml] Carry the assembled sideline screen frame (in folded transport configuration) onto the vinyl and place it face down centered over the material.

+[word/document.xml] Shift the frame until there is an even, equal reveal of perimeter bleed wrap margin on all four sides (top, bottom, left, and right outer rails). Verify that the frame is resting completely square on the vinyl prior to applying any tape.
+[word/document.xml] Step 3: Perimeter Double-Sided Tape Application
+[word/document.xml] Cut sixteen (16) strips of 1-in. heavy-duty double-sided tape, each approximately 4 inches in length.
+[word/document.xml] Apply the tape strips to the rear-facing surface of the perimeter EMT conduit in the following layout:

+[word/document.xml] • Long rails (Top and Bottom A rails): Apply 5 strips spaced evenly along each rail (one centered, two at intermediate quarter points, and two approximately 3 inches inward from the corner brackets; 10 strips total).

+[word/document.xml] • Short end rails (Left and Right B rails): Apply 3 strips evenly spaced along each rail (one centered and two approximately 3 inches inward from the corner brackets; 6 strips total).
+[word/document.xml] Burnish each tape strip firmly onto the conduit surface, then peel and discard the protective release liners from all 16 strips.
+[word/document.xml] Step 4: Long-Side Tensioning and Initial Wrap

+[word/document.xml] Start along one designated long side (typically the top A rail). Beginning at the center tape strip and progressing outward toward both corners, fold the vinyl bleed margin tightly around the conduit and press it firmly into the 5 double-sided tape strips on the rear of the tube. Check that the graphic remains aligned with the outer tubing edge.

+[word/document.xml] Move to the opposing long side (bottom A rail). Starting at the center and working outward, pull the vinyl firmly across the frame face to eliminate all slack and wrinkles. Fold the vinyl edge tightly around the bottom conduit and press it securely into the 5 opposing tape strips.
+[word/document.xml] Sight down the front face beneath the frame: confirm that longitudinal tension is smooth and uniform, with no wave patterns or diagonal wrinkling.
+[word/document.xml] Step 5: Short-Side Dual-Operator Tensioning and Wrap
+[word/document.xml] Station one person at each of the two short end rails (B rails).

+[word/document.xml] Working simultaneously, both operators firmly grasp the vinyl bleed margin on opposite ends and pull outward in opposing directions away from the center. This synchronized outward pull establishes balanced transverse tension across the entire width of the screen without pulling the frame out of square.
+[word/document.xml] While maintaining continuous outward tension, wrap the vinyl edges over the short end rails and press them firmly into the 3 tape strips on each side.
+[word/document.xml] Neatly fold the excess vinyl corner tabs around the corner brackets (F), flattening the material to maintain clean, square corners without bulky bunches.
+[word/document.xml] Step 6: Greenhouse Snap Clamp Installation

+[word/document.xml] Install the 1-in. greenhouse snap clamps directly over the wrapped vinyl at every tape location, pressing each clamp firmly over the conduit until it snaps into full mechanical lock:
+[word/document.xml] • Long rails: Install 5 snap clamps on the top rail and 5 snap clamps on the bottom rail (10 clamps total).
+[word/document.xml] • Short end rails: Install 3 snap clamps on each of the two short end rails (6 clamps total).

+[word/document.xml] The 1-in. greenhouse snap clamps compress the vinyl tightly against the tape and 3/4-in. EMT conduit, providing heavy-duty mechanical clamping that prevents tape peel or edge detachment under stadium wind gusts or rough trailer transit.
+[word/document.xml] Confirm that no snap clamp interferes with the pivoting rear-support G-brackets, bottom support arm clips (I), or corner plugs (H).
+[word/document.xml] Step 7: Final Tension and Mechanical Clearance Inspection
+[word/document.xml] With two operators, carefully lift the completed sideline screen upright off the moving blankets.
+[word/document.xml] Inspect the front vinyl face in bright lighting: verify that the graphic is drum-tight, square, free of wrinkles or sagging, and centered within the visible frame opening.
+[word/document.xml] Verify that all 16 greenhouse snap clamps are fully seated and firmly gripping the conduit over each tape strip.

+[word/document.xml] Deploy the rear support frame (C/D) and engage both bottom support arm clips (I) into the lower inner rail (Figure 8). Confirm that the wrapped vinyl and snap clamps do not bind, rub, or impede frame deployment, clip latching, or folding flat for transport.
+[word/document.xml] Vinyl Removal & End-of-Season Teardown Protocol

+[word/document.xml] CAUTION — Temperature Requirement for Vinyl Removal: Do not attempt removal of the vinyl or adhesive tape unless the ambient temperature is above 80°F (27°C). Attempting to peel the vinyl at lower temperatures will cause the material to tear and permanently damage the custom banner face. In cooler weather, warm the shop or gently heat the taped perimeter with a heat gun on low before peeling.
+[word/document.xml] When taking down screens or preparing frames for graphic replacement:

+[word/document.xml] • Recommended timing (Defer to Band Camp): It is usually much easier to leave the vinyl on the frames over the winter and wait until summer band camp of the following season before attempting removal. Cold late-fall temperatures following competition season make adhesive stiff and brittle, drastically increasing tear risk.

+[word/document.xml] • Solar heating advantage: The warmer it is outside, the better. Staging the screens outdoors in direct sunlight for just a few minutes prior to peeling warms the conduit and softens the tape adhesive, allowing the vinyl and tape to release cleanly and effortlessly with minimal pull resistance.
+[word/document.xml] • Remove greenhouse snap clamps: Carefully pry off all 16 greenhouse snap clamps from the perimeter tubing.

+[word/document.xml] • Peel slowly at shallow angle: Starting at one corner, slowly peel the vinyl wrap back at a shallow angle. Warm adhesive releases cleanly from the bare EMT conduit without pulling the scrim or ink layer.

+[word/document.xml] • Tape stripping & cleanup: Peel remaining tape strips from the conduit. Because the conduit was not aggressively degreased during initial assembly, tape strips will pull off cleanly with minimal adhesive residue.
